name: sgs/nav-drawer
title: SGS Nav Drawer
description: The menu panel the burger opens — on any device (phones, tablets, and desktops when the nav's Burger Menu is set to Always). A full-screen native <dialog> modal (top layer — survives a transformed header ancestor). Its content is editable InnerBlocks (menu, logo, CTA); the × close button is fixed chrome the block always renders. Open/close/focus/scroll-lock/ESC are owned by the shared sgs/nav Interactivity store.

drawerBg.reason: The drawer panel is a disclosure surface toggled open/closed by the burger trigger, not a hover target itself — only its own close button has :hover CSS (style.css:99). Already correctly painted with a real gradient sibling wired (drawerBgGradient, layered over the flat colour rather than replacing it, D-pending: an overlay panel keeps its solid base so alpha in the gradient doesn't let the page behind show through). Confirmed 2026-09-06 (colour-conformance FILL audit).

dialog.label: Drawer container
dialog._note: Root `<dialog>`. Block-private (containerMirror:false, per the render.php header note — a `<dialog>` root falls outside SGS_Container_Wrapper's $allowed_tags, so this mirrors the wrapper's fill/box capability without calling it). drawerBg resolves via explicit attrMap (name doesn't carry a Colour/Background suffix). Border (width/style/colour/colour-gradient/radius) is block-private via `SgsBorderControl` in its own dedicated Border panel (Shape-B migration, matching every other SgsBorderControl-adopting block) — explicitly mapped here because `body` also declares the `layout` cluster these members belong to, and the bare (no-`prefix`) suffix convention could not otherwise tell them apart; the border paints the whole drawer surface, not just `body`'s inner padding. Geometry (position/inset/width/height) is now driven by `anchor` (per-device enum) + `panelSize` (per-device length, trigger/centred only) rather than the retired `edge`/`width` scalars — see render.php's geometry_css_for closure. The WCAG-computed foreground (drawerFgHex) has no independent client-facing attribute — it is always DERIVED from drawerBg, never set directly — so css:color (text cluster) is deliberately NOT declared here.

body.label: Drawer content
body._note: The `.sgs-nav-drawer__body` flex column that hosts the editable InnerBlocks (menu/logo/CTA). Layer GRID because it is the arrangement layer for this composite (flex-direction:column is a fixed style.css invariant, not an attribute — honest gap on css:flex-direction). drawerAlign maps to css:align-items (left/center/right -> flex-start/center/flex-end); drawerGap/drawerPadding are the responsive object-model box members.

close.label: Close button
close._note: The undeletable x close button, fixed chrome rendered as a sibling of $content (FR-36-6). CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (D956): the previous note here claimed toggleCloseColourHover had no per-block attribute behind :hover -- that was stale/wrong. render.php:344 genuinely wires it via sgs_hover_state_rules(), which emits BOTH a touch-guarded :hover rule AND an unguarded :focus-visible colour rule from the same value -- so toggleCloseColourHover controls both states' TEXT colour. Declared here explicitly (base attrMap + states.hover.attrMap) rather than relying on the default {prefix}{suffix} convention, which routed both attrs to the SAME (css:color, element=close, state=NULL) slot with no way to tell them apart -- a real routing-determinism ambiguity (F6 Check #1/#8), not a manifest gap. The button's :focus-visible OUTLINE (border, not colour) remains genuinely uncontrolled by any per-block attribute -- it resolves var(--sgs-focus-color, currentColor) since D467, following the site-wide focus token, which is correct behaviour, just not this element's colour attrs.

decorative.label: Decorative background
decorative._note: The `.{uid}::before` pseudo-element background-media layer. Declared 2026-08-28 to resolve a routing collision: `backgroundImage` and `drawerBgGradient` BOTH resolved to css_property=background-image on css_element=wrapper, identical on every routing axis, so db-consistency reported AmbiguousLayerAttrError (cssprop:ambiguous:sgs/nav-drawer:background-image:OUTER:wrapper::) and the clone-time resolver picked by rowid. They are NOT the same target: render.php:201-210 states the image paints on `.{uid}::before` and NEVER on the dialog root, precisely because the root already carries drawerBg/drawerBgGradient and a background-image there would overwrite the gradient rather than layer with it. Mirrors sgs/container's media-LAYER pattern and reuses the `decorative` element token sgs/cta-section already declares for its identical background-media layer (cta-section.backgroundMedia -> background-image -> decorative). Only backgroundImage is claimed here; the size/position/repeat/attachment companions keep their existing routing.

attributes._comment_closeStyle: Spec 41 FR-41-12 / step 14a: `icon-and-text` is a FOURTH value, ADDED rather than a rename. `separate-x` and `text-swap` are the icon/text DISPLAY axis and do mirror sgs/nav-menu's triggerMode, but `burger-morph` is a GLYPH choice (a CSS-drawn two-bar span, no icon and no text), so re-valuing this enum onto triggerMode's three values would silently delete a shipped look. This enum is REAL and pre-existing; it stays. Its PHP twin is render.php::$sgs_nd_allowed_close_styles and BOTH lists must carry all four values -- a value one side accepts and the other rejects coerces silently, with no error on either side.
attributes._comment_closeLabel_closeIcon: Spec 41 FR-41-12 / step 14a -- the close button's word and glyph, mirroring sgs/nav-menu's triggerLabel / triggerIcon. NEITHER gets a JSON enum (closeLabel is free text; closeIcon is an object), and NEITHER gets a supports.sgs.elements member: they route no CSS property, so an element entry would be a phantom routing slot -- the same ruling Spec 41 section 8.6(e) makes for triggerMode/triggerLabel. The close button's COLOUR is already wired via toggleCloseColour / toggleCloseColourHover / toggleCloseColourGradient on the `close` element and is untouched by this step.

modality.description: D1011: modal (default) uses native showModal() — the visible page is fully inert. non-modal uses show() with freezeBackground()'s selective inert, keeping the header/burger row live and keyboard-reachable while the drawer is open. Never pair non-modal with aria-modal="true" on the dialog — that would hide the deliberately-live header from assistive tech.

backgroundImageDecorative._comment: Spec 35 item 18 / {element}Decorative convention. render.php paints this image as a CSS background (::before layer), never a frontend — the only literal is the operator-only preview thumbnail in edit.js. Default true documents that. When explicitly set false with alt text on the picked image, render.php adds an aria-describedby hidden note to the dialog (the dialog's own aria-label is already claimed for the drawer's accessible name, so the image description is layered on rather than overwriting it).

drawerTextColourHoverGradient.description: Hover-state gradient sibling of drawerTextColourHover. Non-empty wins over drawerTextColourHover on :hover/:focus-visible.

borderColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the border with a masked ring instead of a flat colour (D636 border-gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over borderColour.
